independent_analytic_proof.monotonicity: At date j the coefficient of an earlier common or idiosyncratic normal is respectively sigma*sqrt(dt*rho) or sigma*sqrt(dt*(1-rho)); both are positive. Fixing the other finite coordinates therefore makes every affected exact stock, date basket and Asian average nondecreasing. No digital exponent or clipped-path monotonicity is asserted.
independent_analytic_proof.cap_and_variation: A=(1/nt)*sum_j B_j. On survival every B_j<H, so A<H and 0<=exp(-rT)*max(A-K,0)<(H-K)*exp(-rT)<40. Each coordinate's survival set is an intersection of lower half-lines. Before its endpoint the payoff is nonnegative and nondecreasing; at the strict-knockout endpoint it becomes zero. Its increase plus one downward jump has variation<=2*40=80. Empty/full half-lines obey the same bound. Increasing exact Phi inverse preserves this variation.
independent_analytic_proof.midpoint: On a width-w cell with midpoint m, each half contributes at most (w/2) times its pointwise variation from f(m). The left and right variation sum to the cell variation, including the specified midpoint value. Thus absolute cell quadrature error<=w*TVcell/2. Summing yields TV/(2*N). One-sided endpoint limits define f(0),f(1); endpoint choices have measure zero. Strict midpoint knockout is paid.
independent_analytic_proof.independent_product: Replace independent scalar uniform coordinates by their midpoint grid one at a time. For every fixed choice of all other coordinates, continuous or discrete, the same variation bound holds. Integrating each signed difference and applying triangle inequality gives d*80/(2*2^q). The bounded payoff makes all mixed integrations valid. The normal law here is the exact independent scalar quantile law.
